title: Closed-fibre admissible-modification presentation of open cohomology
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair, with $I$ finitely generated, and let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and define $X',Z',U'$ by base change to $A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-base-change]. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $U$ and $F'$ its inverse image on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For finitely generated ideals $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$, form $B_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, $Z_J=B_J\times_XZ$, and $j_J:U\hookrightarrow B_J$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Order these blowups by domination, identifying ideals giving the same blowup. Their closed fibres form a cofiltered system. The limit of their small etale topoi, denoted $\mathcal T$, has a conservative family of geometric points (compatible geometric points of the closed fibres). Write $p_J:\mathcal T\to (Z_J)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the projections and
$$L^q_F=\varinjlim_Jp_J^{-1}\bigl((R^qj_{J*}F)|_{Z_J}\bigr)\quad(q\geq0).$$
Here $R^qj_*$ is the higher direct image on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the transition maps are the natural pullback/exchange maps. There is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathcal T,L^q_F)\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}(U_{\mathrm{et}},F).$$
Cohomology on a topos means the right derived functors of global sections, as for [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Convergence gives, in total degree $n\geq0$, a filtration with $n+1$ graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Completion identifies $\mathcal T$ with the corresponding limit topos for $(A',IA')$, by the identifications of the closed fibres of corresponding admissible blowups; the blowups extended from $A$ are cofinal among those for $A'$. Under this identification the exchange maps induce a morphism $L^q_F\to L^q_{F'}$ and a morphism of the displayed spectral sequences. On their abutments it is the canonical pullback $H^n(U,F)\to H^n(U',F')$, including the specified filtrations. No isomorphism of the coefficient sheaves $L^q$ or of the abutments is asserted.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373: admissible blowups, (**) and its limit; p.374 final Note for the formal closed-fibre identification.

proof.text: The full-support admissible ideals and their domination order are the filtered preorder of [lem-per-admissible-modification-system]; the same statement supplies the completion comparison of closed fibres. Finite generation and $V(J)=V(I)$ imply $I^N\subseteq J$ for some $N$: choose generators of $I$, powers of each lying in $J$, and expand monomials of sufficiently high degree. Thus the ideals are admissible. Each $B_J\to X$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper], and its inverse image over $U$ is $U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open]. Density needs no density hypothesis on $U\subset X$: [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes $J\mathcal O_{B_J}$ an effective Cartier ideal. On a chart with equation a non-zero-divisor $t$, the complement is $D(t)$ and $R\to R[1/t]$ is injective, since $t^nr=0$ implies $r=0$. This proves schematic density on $B_J$. Hence there is at most one $X$-morphism $b:B_K\to B_J$: it maps $U=B_K\times_XU$ into $U$ by an $X$-morphism, hence by the identity, and two such maps agreeing on the schematically dense $U$ coincide because $B_J$ is proper, so separated, over $X$ [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated]. So composites of domination maps are domination maps and the system is strictly functorial. Since $I$ is finitely generated, $U$ is a finite union of principal affine opens of $X$ and is quasi-compact. The proper $B_J$ and its closed fibre $Z_J$ are qcqs; the open immersion $j_J$ is qcqs as well (both schemes are separated over the affine $X$).

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Put $K_J=Rj_{J*}F$. The Leray specialization of [sk-thm-groth-ss] gives $H^p(B_J,\mathcal H^qK_J)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(U,F)$. Use its canonical truncation-tower realization: apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to global sections and $K_J$, whose cohomology vanishes below zero. Its abutment is identified with $H^n(U,F)$ by the Leray identification in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit]. The filtration is explicitly $F_J^pH^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(B_J,\tau_{\le n-p}K_J)\to H^n(B_J,K_J))$ under that identification. The cited truncation theorem supplies exactness, first-quadrant vanishing, stabilization and the finite filtration. Torsion of each $G_J^q=R^qj_{J*}F$ follows from [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion], taking its set of primes to be all primes and using the qcqs check in Step 1.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Here is the required bounded-below devissage for the affine henselian comparison. Let $z:Z\to X$, and let $C\in D^{\ge0}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ have torsion cohomology. Exactness of $z^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] identifies $z^{-1}\tau_{\le s}C$ with $\tau_{\le s}z^{-1}C$: apply $z^{-1}$ to the kernel and quotient formulas for canonical truncations. Apply the cohomology pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] to every truncation triangle. These maps commute with its boundary: represent a triangle by a mapping cone and the pullback by the unit followed by a comparison of injective resolutions; both commute with the cone differential and shift. The right-derived functors are triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Thus there is a map of the truncation exact couples, hence of their pages by [lem-sp-couple-morphism]. Its $E_2$ map is $H^p(X,\mathcal H^qC)\to H^p(Z,z^{-1}\mathcal H^qC)$, an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-gabber-pair-comparison]. The convergence and stabilization of [thm-sp-truncation-e2] show the stable pages are isomorphic. In degree $n$ there are only $n+1$ filtration pieces; induction on this finite filtration using the short exact sequences of consecutive pieces makes the abutment map an isomorphism. This proves $R\Gamma(X,C)\to R\Gamma(Z,z^{-1}C)$ is a quasi-isomorphism; it does not apply the sheaf theorem directly to $C$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: For a torsion sheaf $G$ on $B_J$, put $h_J:B_J\to X$ and $C=Rh_{J*}G$. Its cohomology is torsion by [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] (all primes), and $C\in D^{\ge0}$. Step 3 therefore applies to this actual complex. In the cartesian closed-fibre square, proper base change [prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change] identifies $z^{-1}Rh_{J*}G$ with $Rh_{J,0*}(G|_{Z_J})$. The Leray identification of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] then gives the isomorphism $H^p(B_J,G)\to H^p(Z_J,G|_{Z_J})$. This is the restriction map itself: pullback is derived unit followed by Leray, and exchange is its adjunction mate, so pasting these two squares gives the unit for $Z_J\to B_J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Apply this to $G=G_J^q$ from Step 2. Relabeling the $E_2$ terms of that existing Leray sequence by these canonical restriction isomorphisms gives the closed-fibre $E_2$ page, without changing its abutment or filtration.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Construct the comparison maps before taking any colimit. Consider either a domination $b:B_K\to B_J$, with $v:U\to U$ the identity, or $b:B'_{JA'}=\operatorname{Bl}_{JA'}(X')\to B_J$, with $v:U'\to U$; here $b$ is the lift $\rho$ of $B'_{JA'}\to X'\to X$ of [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison]. Writing $b_J$ for this map and $b_{KJ}$, $b'_{KJ}$ for the domination maps over $A$ and $A'$, the two $X$-morphisms $b_J\circ b'_{KJ}$ and $b_{KJ}\circ b_K$ from $B'_{KA'}$ to $B_J$ agree, by the uniqueness argument of Step 1 ($U'$ is schematically dense in $B'_{KA'}$ by the Cartier argument of Step 1 over $A'$); so the domination and completion squares commute. Write $j:V\to B$ and $j':V'\to B'$ for the two open immersions and $F_{V'}=v^{-1}F$. The square of these open immersions is cartesian, since the inverse image of the complement of $V(I)$ is the corresponding open complement. Its derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is a map $\beta:b^{-1}K\to K'$, with $K=Rj_*F$ and $K'=Rj'_*F_{V'}$; no invertibility of $\beta$ is required. Exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] gives maps $b^{-1}\tau_{\le s}K=\tau_{\le s}b^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\tau_{\le s}\beta}\tau_{\le s}K'$ for every $s$, and the corresponding maps on shifted cohomology sheaves. Apply $b^*$ on derived global sections [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] followed by these maps. This gives maps of the three vertices of every truncation triangle. They commute with the first two arrows by the kernel/quotient construction; they commute with the boundary by the cone-and-shift argument of Step 3. On taking cohomology these are maps of exact couples, so [lem-sp-couple-morphism] gives maps on all pages, preserving the image filtrations and their stable graded pieces. On $E_2$ the map is exactly pullback along $b$ followed by $H^p(\mathcal H^q\beta)$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Identify the abutment of the map just constructed, including its direction. Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $F\to I$ on $V$ and a resolution $v^{-1}I\to I'$ on $V'$. The termwise exchange formula of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] represents $\beta$ by $b^{-1}j_*I\to j'_*v^{-1}I\to j'_*I'$. Direct images preserve injectives here because their inverse images are exact, as in [sk-thm-groth-ss]; thus global sections of $j_*I$ and $j'_*I'$ compute the two abutments. A section $s\in I^r(V)=\Gamma(B,j_*I^r)$ is first pulled back by the unit for $b$, then sent by underived exchange to its inverse image section on $V'$, and then mapped to $I'^r(V')$. This is precisely the resolution formula for $v^*$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Consequently the abutment map is the identity in the domination case and is $H^n(U,F)\to H^n(U',F')$ in the completion case. Each filtration step is the image of a truncation term mapping to this abutment, so the commutative squares of Step 5 send filtration steps into filtration steps. The graded map is the stable page map by [lem-sp-couple-morphism].

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: The comparisons of Steps 5–6 compose, with the canonical inverse-image associators, by the exchange pasting statement [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] and the composition law for cohomology pullback [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. For the truncation terms this follows by applying the functor $\tau_{\le s}$ to that equality and using its commutation with exact inverse image. Hence the maps of exact couples, and thus of spectral sequences, satisfy the cocycle equations. Restrict the coefficient maps to $Z_K$ or $Z'_{JA'}$; inverse images around these closed-fibre squares compose with the canonical associators. The closed-fibre $E_2$ identifications in Step 4 commute with these maps: expand each as restriction followed by the coefficient map, use the composition law for restriction and naturality in the coefficient morphism in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], and obtain the same two composites. This verifies coherence of the coefficient system and of the stage sequences; it is not an invocation of a Grothendieck comparison theorem requiring an isomorphic exchange.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Use finite sites, not all coverings of the small etale sites. Since $Z_J$ is qcqs, [lem-trf-qcqs-etale-finitary-site] gives the site $E(Z_J)$ of separated etale objects of finite presentation with finite jointly surjective covering families. It has a final object, finite limits, and the same topos as $(Z_J)_{\mathrm{et}}$; base change preserves these finite limits and covers. Its comparison is through the affine basis and the sheaf/cohomology equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos]. The extra finite-limit-closed site is necessary because $Z_J$ itself need not be affine. Associators for base change satisfy the cocycle: each composite is the unique isomorphism of fibre products commuting with all projections. Normalize identity pullbacks to be identities. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-system-strictification] to these sites (use the unique functors to the terminal category as the auxiliary cone). It gives equivalent finite sites whose transition functors compose strictly. Transfer the coefficient maps of Step 7 by these equivalences. This now satisfies the strict hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]. Its colimit site presents $\mathcal T$, the limit topos used in the statement. Finite diagrams descend to a stage by that lemma, so the colimit site has finite limits; its covers are finite stage covers. Thus [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] supplies a conservative set of points. Composing each with the projections gives compatible stage points, represented by geometric points by [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric].

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Take filtered colimits of the exact couples constructed in Steps 2 and 5. Their three exactness equations remain exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Images, kernels and their quotients commute with these colimits (apply exactness to the kernel-image short exact sequences). Hence the spectral sequence of the resulting exact couple has pages $\varinjlim_J E_{r,J}$, by induction on the derived-couple formulas of [def-sp-exact-couple]. At the compatible final objects of the finite sites, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites] identifies its $E_2$ term with $H^p(\mathcal T,\varinjlim_Jp_J^{-1}(G_J^q|_{Z_J}))=H^p(\mathcal T,L_F^q)$. Step 7 supplies exactly the transition formula required there. The colimit couple has $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<0$ and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$. Its canonical abutment is $\varinjlim_JD_J^{0,n}=H^n(U,F)$, because Step 6 makes every transition on this group the identity. By [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] it converges with $n+1$ graded pieces. Its filtration is $F^pH^n=\varinjlim_JF_J^pH^n$, viewed as the union of these increasing subgroups of the fixed abutment. This equality follows from exactness commuting with images; it does not assert equality with each stage filtration.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, admissible blowups and the spectral sequence (**); details of the truncation-tower argument written explicitly.

proof.text: By [lem-per-admissible-modification-system], the completed full-support ideals are cofinal and their closed fibres, including all domination maps, are identified with the original system. Choose the common finite-site models from Step 8 for these identified fibres. They yield the same $\mathcal T$ and projections. The coefficient maps of Step 5 on this common system are the restrictions of $\mathcal H^q\beta$; their coherence was proved in Step 7. Taking their colimit gives $L_F^q\to L_{F'}^q$. The corresponding maps of exact couples induce maps on the filtered colimit couples of Step 9. By [lem-sp-couple-morphism] they give a morphism of the two limit spectral sequences and of their finite filtrations, with the induced map on graded pieces equal to the stable-page map. At every stage Step 6 identified the abutment map with the canonical pullback for $U'\to U$, so the colimit abutment map is that same pullback. This constructs the asserted morphism without making any coefficient-sheaf or abutment-isomorphism claim.
